title: Netanyahu says Israel killed Hamas military leader Mohammed Sinwar
body:
On 28 May 2025, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told parliament that Mohammed Sinwar, believed to lead Hamas's armed wing, had been killed. Listing top Hamas figures killed during the war, he said: "We killed (Mohammed) Deif, (Ismail) Haniyeh, Yahya Sinwar and Mohammed Sinwar." He gave no further details, and Hamas did not confirm the death.

Israeli media reported that Sinwar was the target of an Israeli strike on 13 May 2025 on what the military called a Hamas command center beneath the European Hospital in Khan Younis. The military declined to say whether he had been targeted or killed. According to the Gaza Health Ministry, at least six people were killed and 40 wounded in the strike at the time.

Mohammed Sinwar was the younger brother of Yahya Sinwar, the Hamas leader behind the 7 October 2023 attack, who was killed by Israeli forces in October 2024. Born in 1975 in the Khan Younis refugee camp, he joined Hamas after its founding in the late 1980s and became a member of the Qassam Brigades. He rose to the group's military leadership and was one of the planners of a 2006 cross-border attack in which Israeli soldier Gilad Schalit was captured. Hamas has said Israel targeted him several times, and he was briefly believed killed in 2014. He is reported to have known about the October 7 attack in advance.
